formationLabel: Organized and joined the LCMS 31 December 1903 · first church built 1907 · rebuilt after 1955 flood · active at 350 Millville Avenue
currentUse: Active Lutheran Church—Missouri Synod congregation worshiping at 350 Millville Avenue, Naugatuck, Connecticut. The official LCMS locator lists Sunday worship at 9:15 a.m. year-round and reports 2022 average attendance of 15 and baptized membership of 40; the LCMS New England District gives the same church and address.
summary: St. Paul Lutheran Church in Naugatuck is the continuing Lithuanian-founded Lutheran congregation organized on December 31, 1903 and received into the Lutheran Church—Missouri Synod that same day. Lithuanian Lutherans in Union City built their first church in 1907. The Naugatuck Historical Society records that the Flood of 1955 destroyed St. Paul and that the congregation rebuilt at Millville and Hoadley; Lithuanian heritage field documentation dates the replacement to 1957 and reports reuse of the old cornerstone. The present church at 350 Millville Avenue remains an active LCMS congregation with a current worship schedule. Institution life and building life are therefore separate: the 1903 congregation continued through the destruction of its earlier church into the replacement building. The exact address and parcel of the first church, the deed history, dedicated Lithuanian cemetery, and complete records-custody history remain unresolved.

historicalNarrative.text: St. Paul is a Lithuanian-founded Lutheran congregation in Naugatuck's Union City community, not a same-name Roman Catholic parish or another St. Paul Lutheran church. The Naugatuck Historical Society describes the Lithuanian Lutheran population that established it, while the official LCMS locator fixes the institutional milestone: St. Paul was organized and joined the Lutheran Church—Missouri Synod on December 31, 1903.

historicalNarrative.text: The first church building followed the congregation's organization. Global True Lithuania's field account dates construction to 1907. Because the source does not establish a verified street number or deed parcel and the local historical account identifies the church within Union City without a precise first-site address, this dossier does not import a guessed modern address into the 1907 phase.

historicalNarrative.text: The Flood of 1955 ended the first building's life but not the congregation's life. The Naugatuck Historical Society says the flood destroyed St. Paul and that it was rebuilt at the corner of Millville and Hoadley. Field documentation dates the replacement to 1957 and reports that the old cornerstone was incorporated. That account is treated as building-continuity documentation; it does not create a new parish or imply that every physical component survived.

historicalNarrative.text: The replacement church is the congregation's current home at 350 Millville Avenue. The official LCMS locator lists a year-round Sunday service at 9:15 a.m. and reports 2022 average attendance of 15 with baptized membership of 40. The LCMS New England District independently lists the same congregation and address. These official current sources directly establish both the institution's active status and the building's standing worship use as of the dossier date.

historicalNarrative.text: No merger or successor congregation is needed to explain St. Paul's history: the evidence instead shows institutional continuity through the loss and replacement of a church building. The exact first-site address and title chain, the replacement construction and dedication records, the full congregational register, off-site archival custody, and any dedicated cemetery remain unverified. Active-congregation status does not by itself establish where all historical records are held.

conflictsWithArchiveRecord: The 1903 date is the congregation's official organization and LCMS-reception date; 1907 is a first-building date and must not replace it. The 1955 destruction concerns the earlier church, not the institution, which rebuilt and remains active.
